findings.quote: 記号・数字・色・行為・作品などが、何かの意味や概念を示す / represents a major change
findings.impact: The entry merges actual constitution with symbolism and omits the common proportion construction. Learners cannot distinguish being a change or part of a total from merely signifying one.
findings.evidence: Oxford separates constitution/equivalence and percentage-of-total use; Collins likewise explains change/victory as actual identity. MW has constitute.
findings.action: Give the constitution/proportion meaning explicit separate learner treatment, with matched frames and examples. Move or correctly classify the existing policy-change example, add a proportion-of-total example, and restrict the current not-completely-the-same note to symbolism rather than this meaning.

findings.quote: 表す、象徴する、意味する
findings.impact: Literal depiction of people/scenes and portrayal in an image are not taught. An abstract justice statue and a data graph do not establish the missing distinction.
findings.evidence: All three original dictionaries separately attest pictorial depiction; Oxford also supplies picture/map/data contexts.
findings.action: Add explicit depiction/portrayal treatment with a concrete person or scene example and appropriate active/passive frames. Distinguish a picture of a thing from a symbol of an abstract idea; existing graph material can be mapped coherently to presentation/depiction.

findings.quote: be represented as + 形・記号
findings.impact: The as-pattern is restricted to graphical form, leaving characterization of people/things and self-presentation untaught.
findings.evidence: Oxford/Collins give characterization with O as a person or quality; Collins also lists to be, and MW includes reflexive self-presentation.
findings.action: Explicitly teach describing or presenting O as having a character/status, including an original contextual example and represent oneself as. Keep graphical encoding distinct; qualify register and avoid implying that the asserted characterization must be true.

findings.quote: underrepresented … 十分に代表されていない
findings.impact: A derivative is mentioned but the common be represented in/on meaning of presence/inclusion is missing; readers may assume an individual proxy must be appointed.
findings.evidence: Oxford and Collins have passive presence/inclusion uses; MW expressly includes people and perspectives from a group.
findings.action: Give presence/inclusion explicit treatment with be well/poorly represented in/on and a contextual example. Explain its distinction from having an agent and connect the existing underrepresented note.

findings.quote: No formal statement or to-person/that-clause frame is supplied.
findings.impact: The learner cannot parse a formal representation of concerns or a stated factual claim, despite this being a useful attested construction.
findings.evidence: Oxford lists represent concerns to an authority and represent (to somebody) that; MW/Collins also attest formal stating/protesting.
findings.action: Include concise qualified formal-statement coverage with complete to-person and that-clause frames and an original matched example. Do not infer universal legal warranty effects from the vocabulary.

findings.quote: represent が正しく立場や事実を示す
findings.impact: The contrast falsely builds accuracy into represent, conflicting with ordinary biased or false representations.
findings.evidence: MW and Oxford allow unfair or false characterization; misrepresent explicitly adds misleading/incomplete presentation.
findings.action: Remove the guarantee of correctness. Preserve the useful misrepresent material as a qualified accuracy contrast under the appropriate depiction/characterization use or an explicit usage note.

findings.impact: The sole stand-for example and selected meaning illustrate symbolism, although placed among agency/advocacy synonyms; the definition mixes three senses under one score.
findings.evidence: The article’s flag example matches the symbolic meaning attested in all three represent entries, not acting on someone’s behalf.
findings.action: Move the symbolic comparison to the symbol meaning and narrow its definition there, preserving the example. If a stand-for agency comparison is retained separately, it needs its own matching definition/example and a per-sense score judgment.

findings.quote: exclude / obscure / conceal under 反意語
findings.impact: The current blocks compare agency with exclusion and symbolism with obscuring/concealing, which can coexist rather than oppose each other on the selected sense axis.
findings.evidence: The current definitions/examples operate on participation or disclosure, while the chosen represent blocks describe agency or symbol relations.
findings.action: Reassess the relation axis after the major senses are repaired. Exclude can be compared with the inclusion meaning; retain obscure/conceal as explicit show/hide contrasts only where the selected presentation meaning warrants that axis, otherwise move them to usage. Preserve useful examples without claiming universal antonymy.

contract_observations.observation: Add the existing passive be represented by frame to the grammar overview and Japanese glosses to complete frames; normalize legacy plus/slash placeholders. The company-agent Japanese can be made more natural without changing agency meaning.

Count-noun alternatives need complete articles (a change/an increase/a risk). The graph example is passive but its label is active; align them. The dot example represents ten people, so its label should identify what the symbol stands for rather than describe a percentage/number object.
The stative symbol and constitution readings need appropriate usual non-progressive guidance, scoped so that dynamic representing/depicting uses remain possible.
Clarify underrepresented as insufficient numerical/group presence where appropriate, linked to the new presence/inclusion treatment; the current literal Japanese can suggest inadequate advocacy only.
The main IPA agrees with Oxford. The representation stress shift is correct; no forced phonetic rewrite is needed.
Apply current body heading, frequency syntax, placeholders and line endings while preserving original prompt_version metadata as specifically directed.

independent_coverage_priorities.reason: Repair the clear modern gaps first. Sources differ in splitting; the learner distinctions and complete frames matter more than mechanically reproducing any dictionary’s numbering.

workflow_scope_assessment.reason: The original two-block inventory misses several material modern meanings and constructions. Repair likely needs genuine sense reorganization and multiple explicit units, beyond a small localized correction. Use the normal reevaluation route; do not omit major coverage merely to preserve targeted eligibility.

coverage_notes: All 182 lines and 18 example/translation pairs were inspected. Several core examples are usable but need correct semantic placement.

No numerical frequency changes are demanded by this original assessment. New or separated meanings must receive independent per-sense ordinal judgments, not inherited whole-word scores or fabricated corpus counts.

The public-defender translation was investigated rather than assumed wrong. First-party indexed Japanese government material attests both 公設 and 公選 usages; no claim that 公選 is nonexistent or necessarily means elected is made. A clear generic public-defense gloss may be editorially preferable, but this was not promoted to a false lexical-error finding.
The agency examples contain no detailed rule about appointment, legal eligibility or procedure, so no jurisdiction-specific legal rule was inferred.
limitations: This is a full original assessment, not scoped acceptance or a publication verdict.
No pronunciation audio or measured corpus analysis was performed. Not every comparison term was separately fetched from a dictionary.

Public-defender Japanese references were first-party indexed text only: https://www.moj.go.jp/content/000105603.pdf and https://www.jbaudit.go.jp/koryu/study/pdf/itaku_h27_2.pdf. They were used only to avoid falsely rejecting an attested translation, not as current institutional guidance.
Low-priority theatrical/slang/historical variants were inventoried from major dictionaries but not independently expanded with domain-specific primary research.
conclusion: Eight concrete content findings, including four major coverage gaps, require correction. The normal reevaluation route is appropriate; the existing two-block text is not adequately covered by a small targeted repair.
